body.translated_text: ŚGS 1.1.1: Now, henceforth, we shall explain the <s>pākayajñas</s> (cooked offerings). 1.1.2: One who is about to complete his studentship should kindle the fire on which he would place his last <s>samidh</s> (fuel-stick). 1.1.3: Or the wedding fire. 1.1.4: Some say [the fire should be kindled] at the time of inheritance. 1.1.5: Or, when the householder has died, the eldest [son] himself [kindles it]. 1.1.6: On the new-moon day of <s>Vaiśākha</s>, or on another [new-moon day]. 1.1.7: Some say the <s>nakṣatra</s> (lunar mansion) is chosen at will. 1.1.8: One should kindle the fire from the household of one who is rich in cattle, prosperous in people, distinguished in family, who maintains an <s>ambarīṣa</s> fire, or who is a frequent sacrificer. 1.1.9: Some say [the offerings are made] at evening and morning. 1.1.10: The teachers say that the evening offering has the preparatory rites, and the <s>Adhvaryu</s> is the authority. 1.1.11: In the morning, one should offer the full oblation (<s>pūrṇāhuti</s>) with a <s>Vaiṣṇavī</s> verse, or silently. 1.1.12: The times for its kindling and offering are explained by the <s>Agnihotra</s> (fire ritual). 1.1.13: The rule of being invested with the sacred thread (<s>yajñopavīta</s>) and so forth applies wherever possible, since the ritual system is one. 1.1.14: And they also say: 1.1.15: 'The <s>pākasaṃsthās</s> (cooked-offering rites), the <s>haviḥsaṃsthās</s> (oblation rites), and likewise the <s>somasaṃsthās</s> (Soma rites)—these twenty-one are proclaimed as the forms of sacrifice (<s>yajñasaṃsthā</s>).'

body.translated_text: ŚGS 1.2.0: Now, the feeding of <s>brāhmaṇas</s>. 1.2.1: At the conclusion of a rite, there is the feeding of <s>brāhmaṇas</s>. 1.2.2: Speech, appearance, age, learning, character, and conduct are the qualities [to consider]. 1.2.3: But learning surpasses all others. 1.2.4: One should not pass over learning. 1.2.5: 'Pertaining to the gods, pertaining to the self, pertaining to sacrifice—these three: in the <s>mantras</s> and in the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, this is called learning (<s>śruta</s>).' 1.2.6: 'One who feeds with faith a man who is active in ritual, learned, advanced in sacred knowledge, and ascetic—he will not again suffer hunger.' 1.2.7: 'Whatever deity one wishes to satisfy in all rites, dedicating [the offering] mentally to that deity, one should give in this prescribed manner.' 1.2.8: 'An offering not placed in one of this kind never reaches any deity; this is the treasury of men and is called the vessel of the gods.'

body.translated_text: ŚGS 1.3.1: Now, for the new-moon and full-moon [rites], having fasted: 1.3.2: In the morning, when the sun shines on the tops of the great trees—that is the time for the <s>homa</s> (oblation), the most auspicious time for all the recurrences, except where otherwise prescribed. 1.3.3: Being of good mind, pure, in a clean and secure place, having cooked the <s>caru</s> (porridge offering) according to the full procedure, one offers the <s>sthālīpāka</s> (pot-cooked offering) to the deities of the new-moon and full-moon rites, each according to their share. 1.3.4: In the <s>sthālīpāka</s> offerings, the taking up, placing near, and sprinkling are [performed] according to the <s>mantras</s> and the deities. 1.3.5: And the rules of cutting portions (<s>avadāna</s>) [also apply]. 1.3.6: But before the new-moon and full-moon [main offerings], one should offer to the deities of the inaugural rite (<s>anvārambhaṇīya</s>). 1.3.7: The time for the <s>darśa</s> (new-moon) offering extends until the full-moon day, and the time for the <s>paurṇamāsa</s> (full-moon) offering extends until the new-moon day. 1.3.8: Some consider that the morning oblation at the time of the evening oblation is an overstepping. 1.3.9: But in the <s>Agnihotra</s>, the time is indeed fixed, as shown by the expiatory rites for one who has transgressed the time. 1.3.10: For the daily oblations, one should prepare the offering from rice, barley, or grain husks. 1.3.11: In the absence [of these], something else that is not prohibited [may be used]. 1.3.12: Some say the grains should be washed. 1.3.13: For the other [grains], there is no special preparation. 1.3.14: In the evening, [the offering is] to <s>Agni</s>; in the morning, to <s>Sūrya</s>. 1.3.15: And to <s>Prajāpati</s>, silently, after both [offerings]. 1.3.16: Some [place] a fuel-stick before the morning oblation. 1.3.17: The sprinkling is as prescribed.

body.translated_text: ŚGS 1.4.0: Now, the rules for <s>svādhyāya</s> (Vedic self-study). ŚGS 1.4.1: Having risen in the morning and having sipped water (<s>ācamya</s>), one should study one's own Vedic text (<s>svādhyāya</s>) day after day. ŚGS 1.4.2: [The daily recitation consists of:] '<s>adyā no deva savitar</s>' — two [verses]; '<s>apehi manasas pata</s>' — the [entire] hymn; '<s>ṛtaṃ ca satyaṃ ca</s>' — the hymn; '<s>ādityā ava hi khyata</s>' — the remainder of the hymn; '<s>indra śreṣṭhāni</s>' — one [verse]; '<s>haṃsaḥ śuciṣad</s>' — one; '<s>namo mahadbhyaḥ</s>' — one; '<s>yata indra bhayāmahe</s>' — one; '<s>adha svapnasya</s>' — one; '<s>yo me rājann</s>' — one; '<s>mama agne varcaḥ</s>' — the hymn; and '<s>svasti no mimītām</s>' — and five [verses].

ŚGS_1.5.6: yā.lakṣaṇa.sampannā.syāt /
ŚGS_1.5.7: yasyā.abhyātmam.aṅgāni.syuḥ /
ŚGS_1.5.8: samā.keśa.antāḥ /
ŚGS_1.5.9: āvartāv.api.yasyai.syātām.pradakṣiṇau.grīvāyām /
ŚGS_1.5.10: ṣaḍ.vīrān.janayiṣyati.iti.vidyāt /
body.translated_text: ŚGS 1.5.1: There are four <s>pākayajñas</s> (simple domestic offerings): <s>huta</s> (offered into fire), <s>ahuta</s> (not offered into fire), <s>prahuta</s> (offered by casting), and <s>prāśita</s> (eaten). ŚGS 1.5.2: Five [ceremonies are performed] outside the main hall: the wedding (<s>vivāha</s>), the tonsure ceremony (<s>cūḍākaraṇa</s>), the initiation (<s>upanayana</s>), the end-of-studies hair-cutting (<s>keśānta</s>), and the parting of the hair (<s>sīmantonnyana</s>). ŚGS 1.5.3: Having smeared, swept, and sprinkled [the ground], one should bring forward the fire (<s>agni</s>). ŚGS 1.5.4: Some [say] the fire should be produced by friction (<s>nirmathya</s>) at the wedding. ŚGS 1.5.5: During the northward course [of the sun] (<s>udagayana</s>), in the bright fortnight (<s>āpūryamāṇapakṣa</s>), on an auspicious day, one should take the hand of the maiden. ŚGS 1.5.6: [She] who is endowed with [auspicious] marks. ŚGS 1.5.7: [She] whose limbs are well-formed. ŚGS 1.5.8: [She who has] even hair-lines. ŚGS 1.5.9: If she has two hair-whorls turning clockwise on the neck, ŚGS 1.5.10: one should know that she will bear six heroes.

body.translated_text: ŚGS 1.6.0: Now, the choosing of a bride (<s>kanyāvaraṇa</s>). ŚGS 1.6.1: When about to take a wife, he sends off the suitors [to the bride's family], reciting '<s>anṛkṣarā</s>' [as a blessing for those] going. ŚGS 1.6.2: When going [to the bride's house], they take flowers, fruits, and barley grains, and a water-pot. ŚGS 1.6.3: Having proclaimed three times: '<s>ayam ahaṃ bhoḥ</s>' ('Here am I, sirs!'). ŚGS 1.6.4: After sunrise, those of the groom's family, facing east, and those bringing [the bride], facing west, reciting the <s>gotra</s>-names and personal names [of both families], choose the maiden. ŚGS 1.6.5: When both sides are satisfied, they touch a full vessel (<s>pūrṇapātrī</s>) mixed with flowers, unbroken grains (<s>akṣata</s>), barley, and gold, [reciting:] '<s>anādhṛṣṭam asya anādhṛṣṭyam devānām ojo anabhiśasty abhiśastipā anabhiśaste</s>' — '<s>anyam añjasā satyam</s>' — '<s>upa geṣaṃ suvite mā dhā</s>.' ŚGS 1.6.6: [Reciting] '<s>ā naḥ prajām</s>,' the <s>ācārya</s> (teacher), having risen, places [his hand] on the crown of the maiden's head [saying:] 'I place offspring in you; I place cattle in you; I place brilliance and <s>brahmavarcas</s> (Brahmic splendor) in you.'

body.translated_text: ŚGS 1.7.0: Now, the <s>homa</s> (fire-offering) when consent has been given. ŚGS 1.7.1: When consent is obtained, one offers [into the fire]. ŚGS 1.7.2: Having smeared a square ritual ground (<s>sthaṇḍila</s>) with cow-dung. ŚGS 1.7.3: [Lines are drawn] in the two forward intermediate directions: the southern [line running] eastward for rites to the ancestors (<s>pitrya</s>). ŚGS 1.7.4: The northern [line] for rites to the gods (<s>daiva</s>). ŚGS 1.7.5: Some [say] only the eastern [line]. ŚGS 1.7.6: Having drawn a line running northward in the middle. ŚGS 1.7.7: To its south, one [line] above running upward; one in the middle; one to the north. ŚGS 1.7.8: Having sprinkled those [lines with water]. ŚGS 1.7.9: [Reciting:] '<s>agniṃ praṇayāmi manasā śivena, ayam astu saṃgamano vasūnām, mā no hiṃsīḥ sthaviram mā kumāram, śaṃ no bhava dvipade śaṃ catuṣpade</s>' ('I bring forward <s>Agni</s> with an auspicious mind; may this be a meeting-place of the <s>Vasus</s>; harm not our elders nor our young ones; be beneficent to bipeds and quadrupeds') — thus one brings forward the fire. ŚGS 1.7.10: Or silently. ŚGS 1.7.11: Going clockwise around the fire, one wipes it three times all around with the wet hand — they call this the 'sweeping' (<s>samūhana</s>). ŚGS 1.7.12: Once counter-clockwise for rites to the ancestors (<s>pitrya</s>).

body.translated_text: ŚGS 1.8.0: Now the spreading of sacred grass (<s>paristaraṇa</s>). ŚGS 1.8.1: Now the spreading of sacred grass. ŚGS 1.8.2: He strews around with <s>kuśa</s> grass having their tips pointing eastward, in three layers or five layers. ŚGS 1.8.3: First in front, then behind, then behind again. ŚGS 1.8.4: He covers the roots with the tips. ŚGS 1.8.5: And all the layers, beginning from the south, proceed northward. ŚGS 1.8.6: Having stationed the <s>Brahman</s> priest to the south, [he recites] '<s>bhūr bhuvaḥ svar</s>.' ŚGS 1.8.7: Having adorned [the altar] with flowers. ŚGS 1.8.8: He brings forward the <s>praṇītā</s> waters to the north, [reciting] 'Who leads you forth?' ŚGS 1.8.9: Taking the <s>kuśa</s> grass with the left hand, he sweeps with the right hand. ŚGS 1.8.10: Bending the right knee. ŚGS 1.8.11: The left [knee is bent] in rites for the ancestors (<s>pitrya</s>). ŚGS 1.8.12: There is no constant spreading of sacred grass for <s>ājya</s> (ghee) oblations. ŚGS 1.8.13: But for the regular daily oblations (<s>nityāhuti</s>) also, says <s>Māṇḍūkeya</s>. ŚGS 1.8.14: Having measured with a span a <s>kuśa</s> blade that is fresh, even, with unbroken tip, and without an inner stalk, he cuts it with [another] <s>kuśa</s> blade, [reciting] 'You are purifiers (<s>pavitre stha</s>).' ŚGS 1.8.15: There are two or three [purifiers]. ŚGS 1.8.16: Holding [them] with tips pointing east, he sprinkles [them], [reciting] 'You two belong to <s>Viṣṇu</s> (<s>vaiṣṇavyau</s>).' ŚGS 1.8.17: With two fresh <s>kuśa</s> blades, he sprinkles the fire three times clockwise (<s>pradakṣiṇam</s>). ŚGS 1.8.18: [Reciting] 'You are the milk of the earths (<s>mahīnām payo'si</s>),' he takes up the <s>ājya</s> (ghee) vessel. ŚGS 1.8.19: [Reciting] 'For nourishment, thee (<s>iṣe tvā</s>),' he places it on the fire. ŚGS 1.8.20: [Reciting] 'For vigor, thee (<s>ūrje tvā</s>),' he lifts it off to the north. ŚGS 1.8.21: Holding the purifiers with tips pointing north, grasping from both sides with the thumbs and the ring fingers, having bent them with tips pointing upward, he casts them into the ghee, [reciting] 'With the impulse of <s>Savitṛ</s>, I purify thee with an unperforated purifier, with the rays of <s>Sūrya</s> of <s>Vasu</s>.' ŚGS 1.8.22: The purification of ghee (<s>ājya-saṃskāra</s>) [is to be done] everywhere. ŚGS 1.8.23: One should not offer with unpurified [ghee]. ŚGS 1.8.24: And water [is placed] in the ladle (<s>sruva</s>), [reciting] 'Of <s>Savitṛ</s>, indeed.' ŚGS 1.8.25: These [are used for] the <s>praṇītā</s> and <s>prokṣaṇī</s> (sprinkling) waters.

body.translated_text: ŚGS 1.9.0: Now the ghee oblation (<s>ājya-homa</s>). ŚGS 1.9.1: The ladle (<s>sruva</s>) is the vessel. ŚGS 1.9.2: The taking [of ghee] is determined by the purpose. ŚGS 1.9.3: Taking the <s>kuśa</s> grass with the left hand, [he grasps] the ladle at its base with the right, [reciting] 'You are the hand of <s>Viṣṇu</s> (<s>Viṣṇor hasto'si</s>).' ŚGS 1.9.4: He offers the ghee oblations with the ladle. ŚGS 1.9.5: Beginning from the north-western side of the fire, he offers in an unbroken [stream] to the south, [reciting] 'You, O <s>Agni</s>, are the forethought (<s>pramati</s>).' ŚGS 1.9.6: Beginning from the south-western side of the fire, he offers in an unbroken [stream] to the north, [reciting] 'He whose are these <s>Himavat</s> [mountains].' ŚGS 1.9.7: The northern <s>ājya</s> portion belongs to <s>Agni</s> (<s>āgneya</s>), the southern to <s>Soma</s> (<s>saumya</s>). ŚGS 1.9.8: The other oblations [are offered] in the middle. ŚGS 1.9.9: '<s>Agni</s> is the begetter; may he give me that wife. <s>Svāhā</s>. <s>Soma</s> possesses progeny; may he make me possessed of progeny through her. <s>Svāhā</s>. <s>Pūṣan</s> possesses kinsmen; may he make me possessed of kinsmen through her father, mother, and brothers. <s>Svāhā</s>.' ŚGS 1.9.10: In <s>ājya</s> oblations, the two <s>ājya</s> portions and the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s> [oblation] are not constant. ŚGS 1.9.11: But in the regular daily oblations also, says <s>Māṇḍūkeya</s>. ŚGS 1.9.12: The great <s>vyāhṛtis</s>, all expiatory rites (<s>prāyaścitta</s>), and the <s>prājāpatya</s> [oblation] — this is the place for their insertion (<s>āvāpa</s>). ŚGS 1.9.13: When the offering material is ghee, [he takes] the <s>kuśa</s> blades in the left hand, grasps their tips with the right, [holds] the roots with the left; he smears the tip on the ladle, the middle in the ghee vessel, and the roots also [in the ghee vessel]. ŚGS 1.9.14: But if [he uses] the large ladle (<s>sruc</s>) with rims, [he smears] the tip on the large ladle, the middle on the small ladle, and the roots in the ghee vessel. ŚGS 1.9.15: Having carried them together, [he recites] 'You are the garment of <s>Agni</s> (<s>Agner vāso'si</s>).' ŚGS 1.9.16: Having placed three fuel-sticks (<s>samidh</s>) [on the fire]. ŚGS 1.9.17: The sprinkling is as previously described. ŚGS 1.9.18: For oblations whose <s>mantras</s> are not mentioned but whose deities are specified, he should offer [saying] 'To such-and-such [deity], <s>svāhā</s>; to such-and-such [deity], <s>svāhā</s>' — with a pure <s>svāhā</s>-utterance. ŚGS 1.9.19: The procedure for oblations at the <s>pratiśruta</s> (pledged) fire has been explained.

body.translated_text: ŚGS 1.10.0: Now, the varieties of <s>pākayajña</s> (cooked food offerings). 1.10.1: The basic form is the <s>bhūtikaraṇa</s> (prosperity rite). 1.10.2: And of all <s>ājyāhutis</s> (ghee oblations). 1.10.3: [And the basic form] of the branch [rites] involving animals. 1.10.4: And of the <s>caru</s>-<s>pākayajñas</s> (rice-porridge cooked food offerings). 1.10.5: All these <s>pākayajñas</s> are without <s>prayājas</s> (fore-offerings), without <s>anuyājas</s> (after-offerings), without <s>iḍā</s> (the sacrificial food portion), without <s>nigada</s> (ritual formulas recited aloud), and without <s>sāmidhenī</s> (kindling verses). 1.10.6: On this, there are also verses: 1.10.7: "Offered by the <s>agnihotra</s> oblation, the unoffered is offered in the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>; offered forth by the rites for the ancestors (<s>pitṛkarman</s>), the tasted is offered in the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>." 1.10.8: "With knees not raised and spread apart, one should always offer the <s>havis</s> (oblation); for the gods never accept an oblation offered outside [the prescribed manner]." 1.10.9: "For that which is <s>raudra</s> (pertaining to <s>Rudra</s>), <s>rākṣasa</s> (pertaining to <s>rākṣasas</s>), <s>pitrya</s> (pertaining to the ancestors), <s>āsura</s> (pertaining to <s>asuras</s>), or <s>ābhicārika</s> (pertaining to sorcery)—after reciting the <s>mantra</s>, one should touch water and also touch oneself."

body.translated_text: ŚGS 1.11.0: Now, the <s>Indrāṇī</s> rite. 1.11.1: Now, on that night, [thinking] "tomorrow or the third day they will give away the maiden." 1.11.2: On that night, when the dark period has passed, [they] bathe the maiden including her head with the finest fruits of all herbs, mixed with fragrant substances. 1.11.3: Having dressed [her] in a red or unworn garment. 1.11.4: Having seated the maiden behind the fire, while she is being touched [by the officiant], having offered with the <s>Mahāvyāhṛtis</s> (great utterances), he offers <s>ājya</s>-oblations [saying]: "To <s>Agni</s>, to <s>Soma</s>, to <s>Prajāpati</s>, to <s>Mitra</s>, to <s>Varuṇa</s>, to <s>Indra</s>, to <s>Indrāṇī</s>, to <s>Gandharva</s>, to <s>Bhaga</s>, to <s>Pūṣan</s>, to <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, to <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, to the King, to <s>Pratyānīka</s>." 1.11.5: Four or eight women who are not widows, having satisfied them with vegetable balls, <s>surā</s> (wine), and food, should perform four rounds of dancing. 1.11.6: The same deities [apply] for a male. 1.11.7: [Adding] <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> and <s>Īśāna</s>. 1.11.8: After this, the feeding of <s>brāhmaṇas</s>.

body.translated_text: ŚGS 1.12.0: Now, the marriage rite (<s>vivāhakarman</s>). 1.12.1: Women who are not widows, fortunate, and youthful bring the bathed and auspiciously adorned bridegroom to the maiden's house. 1.12.2: He should not be opposed to them, except regarding forbidden foods and sins. 1.12.3: Having been permitted by them, he then gives a garment to her [reciting] "<s>Raibhy āsīd</s>." 1.12.4: [Reciting] "<s>Cittir ā upabarhaṇam</s>," he takes the ointment box. 1.12.5: [Reciting] "<s>Samañjantu viśve devāḥ</s>" ("May all the gods anoint"), she should be anointed. 1.12.6: [Reciting] "As <s>Śacī</s>, as <s>Vāvātā</s> of good sons, as <s>Aditi</s>, as <s>Apālā</s> who is not a widow—so may this one protect you here," he gives a triple-braided <s>śalalī</s> (hair ornament) in her right hand. 1.12.7: [Reciting] "<s>Rūpam rūpam</s>" ("Form upon form"), [he gives] a mirror in the left [hand]. 1.12.8: Her kinsmen tie a red-and-black woolen or linen thread with three gems as a protective amulet (<s>pratisara</s>), [reciting] "<s>Nīlalohitam</s>" ("Dark red"). 1.12.9: [Reciting] "<s>Madhumatīr oṣadhīḥ</s>" ("Honey-sweet herbs"), he ties <s>madhūka</s> flowers. 1.12.10: At the wedding, having honored [the guests] with a cow, the two <s>mādhuparkika</s> cows [are given] at the house. 1.12.11: Having seated the maiden behind the fire, while she is being touched, he offers three [oblations] with the <s>Mahāvyāhṛtis</s>. 1.12.12: And one should regard the fourth [oblation] with all [three <s>vyāhṛtis</s>] combined, according to this injunction. 1.12.13: Thus, when there is no [specific] instruction, in all prosperity rites (<s>bhūtikarmans</s>), both before and after, one should offer with these same [<s>vyāhṛtis</s>].

body.translated_text: ŚGS 1.13.0: Now, the grasping of the hand (<s>pāṇigrahaṇa</s>). 1.13.1: 'Be queen in your father-in-law's house' — with this [<s>mantra</s>], the father or brother pours [an oblation] on her head from the front with a ladle (<s>sruva</s>), standing, while she is seated, facing east, [he] facing west. 1.13.2: 'I grasp your hand for good fortune' — with the right hand he grasps her right hand, including the thumb, palm upward to palm upward, standing, while she is seated, facing east, [he] facing west. 1.13.3: Having recited the next five [<s>mantras</s>]. 1.13.4: 'I am he (<s>ama</s>), you are she (<s>sā</s>); you are she, I am he. I am heaven, you are earth. You are the <s>Ṛk</s>, I am the <s>Sāman</s>. Be devoted to me.' 'Let us marry here, let us beget offspring, let us obtain sons — may they be many, reaching old age.' Thus. 1.13.5: Having filled a new water-jar [with water, saying] '<s>bhūr bhuvaḥ svar</s>.' 1.13.6: Having placed in it branches with milk-sap, with leaves, and <s>kuśa</s> grass from a tree with a masculine name. 1.13.7: And gold, according to some. 1.13.8: Having given it to a <s>brahmacārin</s> (celibate student) who observes silence. 1.13.9: They stand in the northeast direction; they perform circumambulation (<s>pradakṣiṇā</s>). 1.13.10: And having placed a stone to the north. 1.13.11: 'Come, O beautiful one' — having made her rise. 1.13.12: 'Come, step upon this stone. Be firm like a stone. Overcome the adversaries; vanquish those who contend [against you]' — having her step on the stone with the right fore-foot. 1.13.13: Having led [her] around the fire clockwise. 1.13.14: Having given a second garment with the same <s>mantra</s>. 1.13.15: The father or brother pours parched grains (<s>lāja</s>) mixed with <s>śamī</s> and <s>palāśa</s> [leaves] into her cupped hands (<s>añjali</s>). 1.13.16: And the spreading, pouring over, and counter-pouring with ghee (<s>ājya</s>). 1.13.17: She offers them [into the fire].

body.translated_text: ŚGS 1.14.0: Now, the taking of seven steps (<s>saptapadakramaṇa</s>). 1.14.1: 'This woman approaches, casting parched grains [into the fire]: "May she be auspicious to the kinsmen. May my husband live long!" <s>Svāhā</s>.' Standing, she offers; the husband recites the <s>mantra</s>. 1.14.2: The stepping on the stone and the rest — thus a second time. 1.14.3: Thus a third time. 1.14.4: A fourth time, silently, as desired. 1.14.5: He makes her take seven steps in the northeast direction. 1.14.6: 'For food (<s>iṣa</s>), one step; for strength (<s>ūrja</s>), two steps; for increase of wealth (<s>rāyaspoṣa</s>), three steps; for well-being (<s>āyobhavya</s>), four steps; for cattle (<s>paśu</s>), five steps; for the seasons (<s>ṛtu</s>), six steps; be my companion (<s>sakhā</s>) with seven steps.' 1.14.7: He sprinkles them with water. 1.14.8: Having purified with water for standing, with the three [verses beginning with] '<s>āpo hi ṣṭhā</s>' (O Waters, you are indeed...). 1.14.9: Having sprinkled [water] on the head. 1.14.10: She says: 'I give a cow.' 1.14.11: One should give something to the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s everywhere, in the <s>sthālīpāka</s> (pot-cooked offering) and other rites. 1.14.12: The bridal gift (<s>vādhūya</s>) [goes] to one who knows the <s>Sūryā</s> [hymn]. 1.14.13: A cow is the best [gift] for a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. 1.14.14: A village for a <s>kṣatriya</s>. 1.14.15: A horse for a <s>vaiśya</s>. 1.14.16: A hundred [coins] upon a chariot for one who has a daughter [to give]. 1.14.17: To the sacrificial priests (<s>yājñika</s>s), one gives a horse.

body.translated_text: ŚGS 1.15.0: Now, the departure to the bridegroom's house. 1.15.1: [He recites] the three verses beginning with 'I release you (<s>pra tvā muñcāmi</s>)' when she sets forth from the house. 1.15.2: [He recites] 'Living, weeping (<s>jīvaṃ rudantī</s>)' when she weeps. 1.15.3: Then the wife anoints the chariot axle with ghee, [reciting] 'The axle has become intoxicated (<s>akṣann amīmadanta</s>).' 1.15.4: [Reciting] 'Pure are your two wheels; your two wheels (<s>śucī te cakre; dve te cakre</s>)'—with these two [verses], on the two wheels: the first with the first [verse], the second with the second. 1.15.5: And the two oxen. 1.15.6: [Reciting] 'In the nave of the chariot (<s>khe rathasya</s>),' having driven a peg (<s>śamyā</s>) of a fruit-bearing tree into each of the holes, one each. 1.15.7: Or the permanent [pegs], having recited over them. 1.15.8: Then they yoke the two oxen, [reciting] 'May your right [ox] be yoked (<s>yuktas te astu dakṣiṇa</s>)' with two [verses]; [reciting] 'The two bright draft-oxen (<s>śukrāv anaḍvāhāv</s>)' with this half-verse, he recites over the yoked ones. 1.15.9: Then, if a part of the chariot breaks or is severed, he should bring the maiden into the house of one who maintains the sacred fire (<s>āhitāgni</s>). 1.15.10: [Reciting] 'Cover over with <s>khadira</s> wood (<s>abhi vyayasva khadirasya</s>),' he should repair it. 1.15.11: [Reciting] 'That horse (<s>tyaṃ cid aśvam</s>)' [he ties] the knot. 1.15.12: He mutters the five verses beginning with 'May she fashion auspiciousness for us (<s>svasti no mimītām</s>).' 1.15.13: [Reciting] 'With beautiful <s>kiṃśuka</s> [flowers] (<s>sukiṃśukam</s>)' as she mounts the chariot. 1.15.14: [Reciting] 'May no waylayers find [us] (<s>mā vidan paripanthinaḥ</s>)' at a crossroads. 1.15.15: [Reciting] 'Those who [attend] the bride (<s>ye vadhvāḥ</s>)' at a cremation ground. 1.15.16: [Reciting] 'O lord of the forest, of a hundred branches (<s>vanaspate śata-valśa</s>)' at a great tree, he mutters the half-verse. 1.15.17: [Reciting] 'The good protector (<s>sutrāmāṇam</s>)' when she boards a boat. 1.15.18: [Reciting] 'Full of stones (<s>aśmanvatī</s>)' when she crosses a river. 1.15.19: Or else [she crosses] with the yoked [chariot] itself. 1.15.20: [Reciting] 'Rise up, O wave (<s>ud va ūrmiḥ</s>)' at a deep place. 1.15.22: [Reciting] 'Here is delight (<s>iha priyam</s>),' having arrived at the house after passing seven [houses], the rites are completed.

body.translated_text: ŚGS 1.16.0: Now, the bringing [of the bride] into the house. 1.16.1: It has been stated: 'I have brought [her].' 1.16.2: Having seated her in that [place], while she holds on [to him], the husband offers four oblations. 1.16.3: 'With <s>Agni</s> as the deity, with the earth as the world, among worlds,' with the <s>Ṛgveda</s>, 'among <s>Vedas</s>—with these I pacify you, [O bride]. <s>Svāhā</s>. With <s>Vāyu</s> as the deity, with the atmosphere as the world, among worlds,' with the <s>Yajurveda</s>, 'among <s>Vedas</s>—with these I pacify you. <s>Svāhā</s>. With <s>Sūrya</s> as the deity, with heaven as the world, among worlds,' with the <s>Sāmaveda</s>, 'among <s>Vedas</s>—with these I pacify you. <s>Svāhā</s>. With <s>Candra</s> (the Moon) as the deity, with the quarters as the world, among worlds,' with the <s>Brahmaveda</s> (<s>Atharvaveda</s>), 'among <s>Vedas</s>—with these I pacify you. <s>Svāhā</s>.' 1.16.4: '<s>Bhūḥ</s>! Whatever is your fortune belonging to the husband (<s>patidhnya lakṣmī</s>), whether it slays gods or slays lovers—that I [now] make [auspicious]. <s>Svāhā</s>.' Or, the first [oblation] is accompanied by the first <s>mahāvyāhṛti</s>, the second by the second, the third by the third, and the fourth by all together. 1.16.5: [Reciting] 'Of gentle eye (<s>aghora cakṣuḥ</s>),' he wipes her eyes with the remnant of ghee. 1.16.7: [Reciting] the four [verses] beginning with 'And that divine seed (<s>uta tyā daivyā bhijasā</s>),' followed by the <s>svāhā</s>-utterance at the end, [he pours] the remnant on her head. 1.16.8: Here some bring a boy into her lap, well-born on both sides, [reciting] 'To your womb (<s>ā te yonim</s>).' 1.16.9: Or else silently. 1.16.10: Having placed fruits in his joined palms, he makes her recite an auspicious day-prayer. 1.16.11: 'She will be one who bears sons (<s>puṃśavatī</s>)' [is recited] here. 1.16.12: [Reciting] the remainder of the hymn beginning with 'Here alone remain (<s>iha eva stam</s>),' they bring [her] into the house.

body.translated_text: ŚGS 1.17.1: [Reciting] '<s>dadhikrāvṇo akāriṣam</s>' ('I have praised <s>Dadhikrāvan</s>'), they should both drink curds together. ŚGS 1.17.2: They should sit in silence until the sighting of the Pole Star (<s>Dhruva</s>). ŚGS 1.17.3: After sunset, he shows her the Pole Star, [reciting] 'Be steadfast (<s>dhruvā</s>); may you prosper with me.' ŚGS 1.17.4: She should say: 'I see the Pole Star (<s>Dhruva</s>); may I obtain offspring.' ŚGS 1.17.5: They should observe <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibacy) for three nights. ŚGS 1.17.6: They should sleep on the ground. ŚGS 1.17.7: They should eat curds-and-rice together, [reciting] the three verses [beginning with] 'Drink and be satisfied.' ŚGS 1.17.8: In the evening and morning, they should tend the wedding fire, [reciting] 'To <s>Agni</s>, <s>svāhā</s>; to the non-fire [deity], <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s>, <s>svāhā</s>.' ŚGS 1.17.9: 'May <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s> [grant] a male; may both <s>Aśvins</s> [grant] a male; may <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s> [grant] a male — may a male child grow in me. <s>Svāhā</s>.' — this [verse is recited] first by one desiring a male child. ŚGS 1.17.10: For ten days, there is no departure [from the house].

body.translated_text: ŚGS 1.18.0: Now the fourth-day rite (<s>caturthī karma</s>). ŚGS 1.18.1: Now the fourth-day rite. ŚGS 1.18.2: When the three nights have passed, he offers a <s>sthālīpāka</s> (pot-cooked offering). ŚGS 1.18.3: [With the following verses:] 'O <s>Agni</s>, you are the expiation; you are the expiation of the gods. Whatever form of hers is husband-slaying, remove that from her.' 'O <s>Vāyu</s>, you are the expiation; you are the expiation of the gods. Whatever form of hers is son-destroying, remove that from her.' 'O <s>Sūrya</s>, you are the expiation; you are the expiation of the gods. Whatever form of hers is cattle-destroying, remove that from her.' 'The maiden worshipped the god <s>Aryaman</s> through the fire. May that god <s>Aryaman</s> release her from this [place], not from that [world].' 'The maiden worshipped the god <s>Varuṇa</s> through the fire. May the god <s>Varuṇa</s> release her semen from this [place], not from that [world].' 'The maiden worshipped the god <s>Pūṣan</s> through the fire. May the god <s>Pūṣan</s> release her from this [place], not from that [world].' ŚGS 1.18.4: [The verse] '<s>Prajāpate</s>' [is recited as] the seventh [oblation]. ŚGS 1.18.5: The <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s> (oblation to the fire that has offered well) is the eighth.

body.translated_text: ŚGS 1.19.0: Now, the <s>garbhādhāna</s> (rite of conception). 1.19.1: Having ground the root of an <s>adhyāṇḍa</s> plant, at the time of the fertile season (<s>ṛtuvelā</s>), with the two [verses] '<s>ud īrṣvātaḥ pativatī</s>' ('Rise up from here, O woman with a husband'), ending with <s>svāhā</s>-utterances, he should pour [the mixture] into her right nostril. 1.19.2: [Reciting] '<s>gandharvasya viśvāvasor mukham asi</s>' ('You are the mouth of the <s>Gandharva Viśvāvasu</s>'), he should touch her genital area when about to procreate. 1.19.3: When the act is completed, he should recite: 1.19.4: '<s>prāṇe te reto dadhāmy asau</s>' ('Into your breath I place seed, O such-and-such') — thus he should breathe along [with her]. 1.19.5: 'As the earth is pregnant with <s>Agni</s>, as the sky is pregnant with <s>Indra</s>, 1.19.6: as <s>Vāyu</s> is the embryo of the directions — so I place an embryo in you, O such-and-such.' Or: 1.19.7: 'May the embryo enter your womb — [may] a male [enter] like an arrow into a quiver; 1.19.8: may a hero be born here to you — a son of ten months. 1.19.9: Give birth to a male son; may another male be born after him; 1.19.10: you shall be the mother of those born, and of those you will yet bear. 1.19.11: In the male, in man, [there is] seed; that he pours into woman; 1.19.12: thus <s>Dhātṛ</s> has spoken, thus <s>Prajāpati</s> has spoken. 1.19.13: <s>Prajāpati</s> ordained, <s>Savitṛ</s> fashioned: 1.19.14: he placed a male-[producing element] in other women; he placed a male here. 1.19.15: The auspicious seeds that men generate for us — 1.19.16: by those may you bear a son; be a good bearer, be a milch-cow. 1.19.17: Roar, hold firm, place the embryo, accomplish [it]; 1.19.18: as a bull, O bull, place [the embryo]; we invoke you for offspring. 1.19.19: He whose wife's womb the husband seizes the seed — may a male son be placed in the womb within; 1.19.20: nourish him for ten months within the belly — may he be born the best among his people.' Or [one may use this verse].

body.translated_text: ŚGS 1.20.0: Now, the <s>puṃsavana</s> (rite for producing a male child). 1.20.1: In the third month, the <s>puṃsavana</s> [is performed]. 1.20.2: Under the <s>nakṣatra</s> (lunar mansion) of <s>Puṣya</s> or <s>Śravaṇa</s>. 1.20.3: Having ground a <s>Soma</s> shoot, or a thorn of <s>kuśa</s> grass, or the last sprout of a branch of a <s>nyagrodha</s> (banyan) tree, or the tip of a sacrificial post (<s>yūpa</s>). 1.20.4: Or, at the conclusion of a sacrifice, the remnant drippings (<s>saṃsrāva</s>) of the offering ladles. 1.20.5: [Reciting] '<s>agninā rayim</s>' ('Through <s>Agni</s>, wealth'), '<s>tan nas turīpam</s>' ('That [protection] for us'), '<s>samiddha agnir vanavat</s>' ('The kindled <s>Agni</s>, like a forest'), '<s>piśaṅga rūpa</s>' ('Of tawny form') — with these four [verses], ending with <s>svāhā</s>-utterances, he should pour [the mixture] into her right nostril.

body.translated_text: ŚGS 1.21.0: Now, the <s>garbharakṣaṇa</s> (protection of the embryo). 1.21.1: In the fourth month, the <s>garbharakṣaṇa</s> [is performed]. 1.21.2: [Reciting] '<s>brahmaṇā agniḥ saṃvidāna</s>' ('May <s>Agni</s>, in accord with <s>Brahman</s>') — having offered the six [oblations] of the <s>sthālīpāka</s> (pot-cooked offering). 1.21.3: [Reciting] '<s>akṣībhyām te nāsikābhyām</s>' ('From your eyes, from your nostrils') — with each verse, having smeared the limbs [of the woman] with an anointing of ghee.

body.translated_text: ŚGS 1.22.0: Now, the <s>sīmantonnyana</s> (parting of the hair). 1.22.1: In the seventh month during the first pregnancy, [one performs] the <s>sīmantonnyana</s>. 1.22.2: Having bathed [the wife] and dressed [her] in an unworn garment, he seats her behind the fire. 1.22.3: While she is being touched [by him], he offers with the great <s>vyāhṛtis</s> (<s>mahāvyāhṛtis</s>). 1.22.4: Having cooked a <s>sthālīpāka</s> (pot-cooked offering). 1.22.5: Some [say] a mung-bean porridge (<s>mudga-odana</s>). 1.22.6: The implements and the <s>nakṣatra</s> (lunar mansion) should be those [suited] for a male [child]. 1.22.7: [He recites:] '<s>Dhātā dadātu dāśuṣe prācīṃ jīvātuṃ akṣitim / vayaṃ devasya dhīmahi sumatiṃ satyadharmaṇaḥ</s>' ('May <s>Dhātṛ</s> give to the worshipper an imperishable life reaching eastward; may we obtain the favor of the god whose law is truth.') '<s>Dhātā prajāyā uta rāya īśe, dhātā idaṃ viśvaṃ bhuvanaṃ jajāna / dhātā putraṃ yajamānāya dātā, tasmā u havyaṃ ghṛtavaj johota</s>' ('<s>Dhātṛ</s> rules over offspring and over wealth; <s>Dhātṛ</s> gave birth to this entire world; <s>Dhātṛ</s> will give a son to the sacrificer; to him therefore offer the oblation rich in ghee.') [Then reciting] '<s>nejameṣa parā pata</s>' — three [verses]; '<s>prajāpata</s>' — the sixth [verse]. 1.22.8: Three times, with a white porcupine quill (<s>śvetā śalalī</s>) or a <s>darbha</s>-grass needle, together with <s>udumbara</s> splints, he parts her hair upward from the middle, [reciting] '<s>bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ</s>.' 1.22.9: Having placed [the splints and quill] in her lap. 1.22.10: He ties a triple-braided [cord] around her neck, [reciting] '<s>ayam ūrjāvato vṛkṣa, ūrjīva phalinī bhava</s>' ('This tree is full of sap; be fruitful like it, full of vigor'). 1.22.11: Then he says to the <s>vīṇā</s> (lute) singers: 'Sing [the praises of] a king,' [reciting] '<s>yo vā apy anyo vīrataraḥ</s>' ('Or whoever else is more heroic'). 1.22.12: Having cast unbroken grains into a water vessel, [he recites] '<s>Viṣṇur yoniṃ kalpayatu</s>' ('May <s>Viṣṇu</s> prepare the womb'), '<s>Rākām aham</s>' [etc.]. 1.22.13: He should make her drink [the water] with a hymn of six verses. 1.22.14: Then he should touch her belly. 1.22.15: [Reciting:] 'You are a <s>suparṇa</s> (eagle), you are <s>Garutmān</s>; the <s>trivṛt</s> is your head, the <s>gāyatrī</s> is your eye; the meters (<s>chandas</s>) are your limbs, the <s>yajus</s>-formulas are your name, the <s>sāman</s> is your body.' 1.22.16: He should have her listen to a joyful song. 1.22.17: Or the great song of the <s>Himavat</s>. 1.22.18: A bull is the priestly fee (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>).

body.translated_text: ŚGS 1.23.0: Now, the smearing of the birth-room (<s>sūtikāgṛha</s>). 1.23.1: Having ground the roots of <s>kākātanī</s>, <s>macakacātanī</s> (both being plants that drive away [evil spirits]), <s>kośātakī</s> (Luffa), <s>bṛhatī</s> (Solanum), and <s>kālakītaka</s> (a black insect-repelling herb), one should smear the place where [the woman] will give birth, for the warding off of <s>rākṣasas</s> (demons).

body.translated_text: ŚGS 1.24.0: Now, the birth rite (<s>jātakarman</s>). 1.24.1: Now, the birth rite. 1.24.2: Having breathed over the newborn child three times, he should make it breathe along [reciting]: "Breathe with the <s>Ṛk</s>, breathe together with the <s>Yajus</s>, breathe up with the <s>Sāman</s>." 1.24.3: Having mixed ghee and honey, curd and water, or having ground rice and barley, he should feed [the child] three times with [a spoon of] gold. 1.24.4: "I offer to you what is sweet with honey, for the sake of the sacrifice, produced by <s>Savitṛ</s>, with the bountiful one. May you, long-lived, guarded by the gods, live a hundred autumns in this world." 1.24.4 [cont.]: He gives a name to the child, "So-and-so," [a name that is] beginning with a sonorous [consonant], having a semivowel in the middle, of two syllables or four syllables, or even of six syllables; it should be a formed [kṛt-derivative], not a secondary derivative (<s>taddhita</s>). 1.24.5: That [secret name], only the father and mother should know. 1.24.6: On the tenth day, [he gives] the public name, one pleasing to <s>brāhmaṇas</s>. 1.24.7: Having made an ink from the hairs of a black cow—white, black, and red [hairs]—and having mixed it in this same group of four [substances], he should feed [the child] four [times]—thus [says] <s>Māṇḍūkeya</s>. 1.24.8: "<s>Bhūḥ</s>, the <s>Ṛgveda</s>—'I place in you, so-and-so. <s>Svāhā</s>.' <s>Bhūr bhuvaḥ svar</s>—speech, sentences, <s>Itihāsa</s>, <s>Purāṇa</s>. <s>Oṃ</s>—all the <s>Vedas</s> I place in you, so-and-so. <s>Svāhā</s>."—or thus. 1.24.9: For generating intelligence (<s>medhājanana</s>), [he whispers] in the right ear "<s>Vāk</s>" (Speech) three times. 1.24.10: "The goddess <s>Vāk</s> (Speech), in accord with the mind, proclaimed by <s>Indra</s> together with <s>Prāṇa</s> as her calf—may the goddess, great, resounding, watery, self-born <s>Vāṇī</s> (Voice) be pleased with you for the sake of good cheer"— 1.24.10 [cont.]: with this [<s>mantra</s>] he should consecrate [the child]. 1.24.11: Having tied gold with a hemp thread [in the manner of] <s>jātarūpa</s> (native gold), 1.24.12: he fastens it on the right hand until the [first] rising [of the child]. 1.24.13: After the tenth day, he should give [it] to <s>brāhmaṇas</s>. 1.24.14: Or he may perform [the rite] at home.

body.translated_text: ŚGS 1.25.0: Now, the naming ceremony (<s>nāmakarman</s>). 1.25.1: On the tenth night, the rising [ceremony]. 1.25.2: The mother and father bathe their heads and wear unworn garments. 1.25.3: And [so does] the child. 1.25.4: In this very <s>sūtikā</s> fire (the birth-chamber fire), having cooked a <s>sthālīpāka</s> (pot-cooked offering): 1.25.5: having offered [oblations] on the birth <s>tithi</s> (lunar day), and [on] three <s>nakṣatras</s> (lunar mansions) together with their presiding deities; 1.25.6: among those, he should offer in the middle to the one [<s>nakṣatra</s>] under which [the child] was born, but the deity [oblation] always first. 1.25.7: "May this excellent <s>Agni</s> [grant] you life today with songs; give us life to live; O <s>Agni</s>, giver of life, growing with the oblation, 1.25.7 [cont.]: with a ghee-face, ghee-born, be [so]; having drunk ghee and the sweet, beautiful [milk of] cows—O <s>Soma</s>, [grant us] great fortune." "Like a father his son, may he protect this one here." 1.25.7 [cont.]: [This is] the tenth-day <s>sthālīpāka</s>. 1.25.8: Having proclaimed the name publicly. 1.25.9: Having had the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> pronounce blessings (<s>svasti</s>). 1.25.10: In the same manner, month by month, having offered on the birth <s>tithi</s>. 1.25.11: After a year, he offers in the domestic fire (<s>gṛhya agni</s>).

body.translated_text: ŚGS 1.27.0: Now the first feeding of solid food (<s>annaprāśana</s>). ŚGS 1.27.1: In the sixth month, the first feeding of solid food [takes place]. ŚGS 1.27.2: [He feeds the child] goat's meat if he desires food. ŚGS 1.27.3: Partridge meat if he desires <s>brahmavarcas</s> (Brahmic splendor). ŚGS 1.27.4: Fish if he desires swiftness. ŚGS 1.27.5: Rice cooked in ghee if he desires radiance (<s>tejas</s>). ŚGS 1.27.6: He should feed [the child] food mixed with curds, honey, and ghee. ŚGS 1.27.7: [Reciting:] 'O lord of food (<s>Annapati</s>), give us food that is free from disease and full of vigor; advance the giver onward; grant us strength for bipeds and [quadrupeds].' [And:] '<s>yac cid dhi</s>' [and] '<s>mahaś cit</s>.' 'O <s>Agni</s>, for this one's long life, splendor, and sharp vigor; O <s>Varuṇa</s>, O <s>Soma</s>, O king, may <s>Aditi</s> grant him protection like a mother; may all the gods [grant] that he reach old age' — having offered thus. ŚGS 1.27.8: Having consecrated [the food by reciting] '<s>agna āyūṃṣi</s>' ('O <s>Agni</s>, [grant] long lives'). ŚGS 1.27.9: Having seated [the child] on <s>kuśa</s> grass with tips pointing north, [reciting] 'O Earth, be gentle (<s>syonā pṛthivi bhava</s>).' ŚGS 1.27.10: The feeding is [done] with the great <s>vyāhṛtis</s> (<s>bhūḥ</s>, <s>bhuvaḥ</s>, <s>svaḥ</s>). ŚGS 1.27.11: The mother should eat the remainder.

body.translated_text: ŚGS 1.28.0: Now, the <s>cūḍākarma</s> (tonsure ceremony). 1.28.1: The <s>cūḍākarma</s> [is performed] in the first year. 1.28.2: Or in the third year. 1.28.3: In the fifth year for a <s>kṣatriya</s>. 1.28.4: In the seventh year for a <s>vaiśya</s>. 1.28.5: Having set up the fire. 1.28.6: And having filled vessels with rice, barley, sesame, and black beans. 1.28.7: Having placed to the north, for receiving the hair: bull's dung, a split <s>kuśa</s> blade, a mirror, fresh butter, a metal razor. 1.28.8-verse: 'Mingle together, O waters rich in truth, most sweet with your waves; mixing milk with honey, delightful, for the winning of wealth.' 1.28.8: He pours cold [water] into the hot water. 1.28.9-verse: 'May the waters moisten [him] for life, for long life, for splendor. The triple lifespan of <s>Jamadagni</s>, the triple lifespan of <s>Kaśyapa</s>, the triple lifespan of <s>Agastya</s>, the triple lifespan that is of the gods—that triple lifespan I bestow upon you.' 1.28.9: [Calling him] by name, with the cold and hot water he moistens the right side of the hair three times. 1.28.10: Some [separate the hair] with a porcupine quill, having untangled it. 1.28.11: Having anointed [the hair] with fresh butter. 1.28.12: [Reciting] 'O herb, protect him (<s>oṣadhe trāyasva enam</s>),' he places a fresh <s>kuśa</s> blade in between. 1.28.13: Having touched the hair and the fresh <s>kuśa</s> blade with the mirror. 1.28.14: [Reciting] 'You are radiance; your father is the axe; do not harm him (<s>tejo'si svadhitis te pitā mā enaṃ hiṃsīḥ</s>),' he takes up the metal razor. 1.28.15: 'With which <s>Savitṛ</s> shaved the beard at first, with which razor the wise [<s>Savitṛ</s>] shaved king <s>Varuṇa</s>'s [beard], with which <s>Dhātṛ</s> and <s>Bṛhaspati</s> shaved the head of <s>Indra</s>—with that, O <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, shave this one today. May he be long-lived, of long life, may this hero be [named] so-and-so'—he cuts the tips of the hair and the fresh <s>kuśa</s> blade. 1.28.16: Thus a second time, thus a third time. 1.28.17: Thus twice more on the northern [side]. 1.28.18: On the sides under the arms, the sixth and seventh [cuttings are performed] at the <s>godāna</s> (cow-giving) ceremony. 1.28.19: This <s>godāna</s> ceremony is indeed the same as the <s>cūḍākarma</s>. 1.28.20: [It is performed] in the sixteenth or eighteenth year. 1.28.21: But at the third shaving, he gives a cow and an unworn garment. 1.28.22: For girls, [the ceremony is performed] silently and with covering. 1.28.23: In the northeastern direction, in a place rich in herbs, or near water, they bury the [cut] hair. 1.28.24: To the barber, the vessels of grain; to the barber, the vessels of grain.

body.translated_text: ŚGS 2.1.0: Now, the <s>upanayana</s> (initiation). 2.1.1: One should initiate a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> in the eighth year from conception. 2.1.2: With the skin of a black antelope (<s>aiṇeya ajina</s>). 2.1.3: Or in the tenth year from conception. 2.1.4: A <s>kṣatriya</s> in the eleventh year from conception, with the skin of a <s>ruru</s> deer. 2.1.5: A <s>vaiśya</s> in the twelfth year from conception, with a cowhide. 2.1.6: Up to the sixteenth year for a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, the time has not passed. 2.1.7: Up to the twenty-second for a <s>kṣatriya</s>. 2.1.8: Up to the twenty-fourth for a <s>vaiśya</s>. 2.1.9: After that, they become <s>patitasāvitrīkas</s> (fallen from the <s>Sāvitrī</s> [initiation]). 2.1.10: One should not initiate them. 2.1.11: One should not teach them. 2.1.12: One should not officiate at their sacrifices. 2.1.13: One should not transact with them. 2.1.14: All should wear girdles, [clothed] in unworn [garments]. 2.1.15: The girdle of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> is of <s>muñja</s> grass. 2.1.16: That of a <s>kṣatriya</s> is a bowstring. 2.1.17: That of a <s>vaiśya</s> is of wool thread. 2.1.18: The staff of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> is of <s>palāśa</s> (Butea) or <s>bilva</s> (wood-apple). 2.1.19: That of a <s>kṣatriya</s> is of <s>nyagrodha</s> (banyan). 2.1.20: That of a <s>vaiśya</s> is of <s>udumbara</s> (fig). 2.1.21: [The staff] of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> reaches to the nose (<s>prāṇasammita</s>). 2.1.22: That of a <s>kṣatriya</s> reaches to the forehead. 2.1.23: That of a <s>vaiśya</s> reaches to the hair. 2.1.24: Or all [types] for all. 2.1.25: Whichever [items] he does not bind on, that is at the teacher's discretion. 2.1.26: Having had the hair shaved (<s>parivāpya</s>), the candidate should be initiated. 2.1.27: Having bathed and adorned [himself]. 2.1.28: Having offered [into the fire], the two stand behind the fire—the <s>ācārya</s> (teacher) facing east, the other facing west. 2.1.29: Standing, he should initiate the one who is standing. 2.1.30: [Reciting:] '<s>Mitrasya cakṣur dharuṇaṃ balīyas, tejo yaśasvi sthaviram samṛddham / anāhanasyam vasanaṃ cariṣṇu, pari idam vājy ajinaṃ dadhe aham</s>' ('The eye of <s>Mitra</s>, the sustaining, the mightier, the splendid, the glorious, the firm, the prosperous—an indestructible garment, fit for movement—I put on this vigorous skin').

body.translated_text: ŚGS 2.2.1: [Reciting:] '<s>Iyaṃ duruktāt paribādhamānā varṇaṃ pavitraṃ punatī na āgāt / prāṇāpānābhyāṃ balam āviśantī sakhā devī subhagā mekhalā iyam</s>' ('This [girdle], warding off evil speech, has come purifying the complexion as a purifier; entering with strength through <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s>, this girdle is a divine friend, bringing good fortune')—winding the girdle three times clockwise, he wraps it around three times. 2.2.2: One knot, or three, or five. 2.2.3: Having made the sacred thread (<s>yajñopavīta</s>), [he recites:] 'You are the sacred thread; you are the sacred thread of the sacrifice; with the sacred thread of the sacrifice I bind you.' 2.2.4: Having filled [the student's] cupped hands [with water], he then says to him: 'What is your name?' 2.2.5: 'I am so-and-so, sir' — the other [replies]. 2.2.6: 'Of the same lineage (<s>samānārṣeya</s>)' — the <s>ācārya</s> [says]. 2.2.7: 'I am of the same lineage, sir' — the other [replies]. 2.2.8: 'Be a <s>brahmacārin</s> (celibate student)! Speak [the vow]!' 2.2.9: 'I am a <s>brahmacārin</s>, sir' — the other [replies]. 2.2.10: [Reciting] '<s>bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ</s>,' he pours three handfuls of water into his cupped hands. 2.2.11: Grasping his hands with both the right and left hands, he recites: 2.2.12: 'By the impulse of the god <s>Savitṛ</s>, with the arms of the two <s>Aśvins</s>, with the hands of <s>Pūṣan</s>, I initiate you, so-and-so.' 2.2.13: [Reciting] '<s>gaṇānāṃ tvā</s>' ('You of the hosts')—for those who desire followers. 2.2.14: [Reciting] '<s>gā gantā mā riṣaṇyata</s>' ('Go forth, cattle, may you not be harmed')—for warriors. 2.2.15: With the <s>mahāvyāhṛtis</s>—for those who are afflicted.

body.translated_text: ŚGS 2.3.1a: "<s>Bhaga</s> has grasped your hand, <s>Savitṛ</s> has grasped your hand, <s>Pūṣan</s> has grasped your hand, <s>Aryaman</s> has grasped your hand. You are <s>Mitra</s> by law (<s>dharma</s>); <s>Agni</s> is your teacher." 2.3.1b: "So-and-so, I and you both—O <s>Agni</s>, I entrust to you this <s>brahmacārin</s> (Vedic student); O <s>Indra</s>, I entrust to you this <s>brahmacārin</s>; O <s>Āditya</s>, I entrust to you this <s>brahmacārin</s>; O <s>Viśve Devāḥ</s> (All-gods), I entrust to you this <s>brahmacārin</s>—for long life, for good offspring, for manly vigor, for increase of wealth, for sovereignty over all the <s>Vedas</s>, for good renown, and for welfare." 2.3.2: [Reciting] "I have turned the turning of <s>Indra</s>, I have followed the turning of <s>Āditya</s>," he wraps around the right arm. 2.3.3: Having stroked the right shoulder with the right span of the hand, [reciting] "May I be dear to your heart, O you who will not be harmed," he touches the region of the heart. 2.3.4: Silently, [he turns] counter-clockwise. 2.3.5: Then, placing his hand with upraised fingers on [the student's] heart, he mutters:

ŚGS_2.4.6: <.eṣā.te.agne.samid>.iti.abhyādadhāti.samidham.tūṣṇīm.vā /
body.translated_text: ŚGS 2.4.1: "In my vow I place your heart; may your thought follow my thought. May you, with single mind, delight in my speech. May <s>Bṛhaspati</s> yoke you to me." 2.4.2: "For the sake of desire, of <s>brahmacarya</s> (sacred studentship), so-and-so." 2.4.3: With the same <s>mantra</s>, having turned around in the same way, 2.4.4: having grasped the right shoulder with the right span of the hand, he mutters: 2.4.5: "You are a <s>brahmacārin</s>. Place fuel [on the fire]. Drink water. Perform service. Do not sleep during the day. Restrain your speech, from the placing of the fuel-stick onward." 2.4.6: [Reciting] "This, O <s>Agni</s>, is your fuel-stick," he places a fuel-stick [on the fire]—or silently.

body.translated_text: ŚGS 2.5.0: Now, the instruction of the <s>Sāvitrī</s> [verse]. 2.5.1: After a year, he teaches the <s>Sāvitrī</s>. 2.5.2: [Or] after three nights. 2.5.3: Or immediately [after initiation]. 2.5.4: He should recite the <s>Gāyatrī</s> [meter] to a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. 2.5.5: The <s>Triṣṭubh</s> to a <s>kṣatriya</s>. 2.5.6: The <s>Jagatī</s> to a <s>vaiśya</s>. 2.5.7: But [in any case], the <s>Sāvitrī</s> itself [is to be taught]. 2.5.8: They sit to the north of the fire. 2.5.9: The <s>ācārya</s> (teacher) faces east, the other faces west. 2.5.10: Having said "<s>Adhīhi bhoḥ</s>" ("Teach, sir!"), 2.5.11: the <s>ācārya</s>, having uttered the syllable <s>Oṃ</s>, then makes the other recite, [saying] "O sir, recite the <s>Sāvitrī</s>." 2.5.12: Then he teaches him the <s>Sāvitrī</s>: "<s>Tat savitur vareṇyam</s>" ("That excellent [glory] of <s>Savitṛ</s>")—this [verse], foot by foot, [then] half-verse by half-verse, without a break.

ŚGS_2.6.7: ācāryāya.bhaikṣyam.nivedayitvā.anujñāto.guruṇā.bhuñjīta /

body.translated_text: ŚGS 2.6.0: Now, the observances (<s>vrata</s>). 2.6.1: "You are called Waters; you are called Auspicious; you are called Nourishing; you are called Ageless; you are called Fearless; you are called Immortal—'May I partake of your goodwill; place me [therein]'"—thus, having made [the student] sip water three times. 2.6.2: [Reciting] "May [the deities] measure out welfare for us (<s>svasti no mimītām</s>)," with the hymn of five verses, he gives [the student] the staff (<s>daṇḍa</s>). 2.6.3: A choice [garment is] the priestly fee (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>). 2.6.4: Having led [the student] clockwise around the fire, he goes to beg alms in the village. 2.6.5: But first from his mother. 2.6.6: Or from one who would not refuse him. 2.6.7: Having reported the alms to the <s>ācārya</s> (teacher) and being permitted by the <s>guru</s>, he should eat. 2.6.8: Day after day, the placing of the fuel-stick (<s>samidādhāna</s>), the going for alms (<s>bhikṣācaraṇa</s>), sleeping on the ground (<s>adhaḥśayyā</s>), and service to the <s>guru</s> (<s>guruśuśrūṣā</s>)—these are the constant duties of the <s>brahmacārin</s>.

body.translated_text: ŚGS 2.7.0: Now, the <s>anuvacana</s> (recitation/instruction). 2.7.1: Now, [the rules] for the recitation [of the <s>Veda</s>]. 2.7.2: They sit to the north of the fire. 2.7.3: The <s>ācārya</s> (teacher) faces east; the other [i.e., the student] faces west. 2.7.4: Having saluted and grasped the feet of the <s>ācārya</s>, and having washed [the teacher's] hands. 2.7.5: Pressing with the right knee upon <s>kuśa</s> grass blades at their root. 2.7.6: Grasping [them] in the middle with both the right and left hands. 2.7.7: The <s>ācārya</s>, taking hold of the tips with the left [hand] and sprinkling with water with the right, then causes the other [student] to recite. 2.7.8: 'Sir, recite the <s>Sāvitrī</s> for me' — [says] the other [student]. 2.7.9: 'I recite the <s>Sāvitrī</s> for you' — [says] the <s>ācārya</s>. 2.7.10: 'Sir, recite the <s>Gāyatrī</s> for me' — the other [says]. 'I recite the <s>Gāyatrī</s> for you' — the <s>ācārya</s> [says]. 2.7.11: 'Sir, recite the [verse] of <s>Viśvāmitra</s> for me' — the other [says]. 'I recite the [verse] of <s>Viśvāmitra</s> (or <s>Vaiśvānara</s>) for you' — the <s>ācārya</s> [says]. 2.7.12: 'Sir, recite the <s>ṛṣis</s> (seers) for me' — the other [says]. 'I recite the deities for you' — the <s>ācārya</s> [says]. 2.7.13: 'Sir, recite the deities for me' — the other [says]. 'I recite the deities for you' — the <s>ācārya</s> [says]. 2.7.14: 'Sir, recite the meters (<s>chandas</s>) for me' — the other [says]. 'I recite the meters for you' — the <s>ācārya</s> [says]. 2.7.15: 'Sir, recite the <s>śruti</s> (revealed scripture) for me' — the other [says]. 'I recite the <s>śruti</s> for you' — the <s>ācārya</s> [says]. 2.7.16: 'Sir, recite the <s>smṛti</s> (tradition) for me' — the other [says]. 'I recite the <s>smṛti</s> for you' — the <s>ācārya</s> [says]. 2.7.17: 'Sir, recite faith and intellect (<s>śraddhā</s>, <s>medhā</s>) for me' — the other [says]. 'I recite faith and intellect for you' — the <s>ācārya</s> [says]. 2.7.18: In this manner, for whichever seer's (<s>ṛṣi</s>'s) <s>mantra</s>, whichever deity, and whichever meter — accordingly he should recite that <s>mantra</s>. 2.7.19: Or, if one does not know the <s>ṛṣi</s>, deity, and meter, [he should recite] '<s>tat savitur vareṇyam</s>' — this [<s>Sāvitrī</s>], one quarter-verse at a time without stopping; 'This is it' — the <s>ācārya</s> says when completed. 2.7.20: Thus one should recite one <s>ṛṣi</s> [at a time], or one <s>anuvāka</s> (section). 2.7.21: For the minor hymns (<s>kṣudrasūktas</s>), an <s>anuvāka</s> [at a time]. 2.7.22: Or as much as the <s>guru</s> thinks fit. 2.7.23: At the first and last [hymns], or at a desired hymn of the <s>ṛṣi</s>, one may recite. 2.7.24: Or of the <s>anuvāka</s>. 2.7.25: One [verse] at a time at the beginning of a hymn. 2.7.26: 'This is the beginning' — at the beginning of any hymn the <s>ācārya</s> [says]. 2.7.27: This has been explained in the chapter on the <s>ṛṣi</s>-<s>svādhyāya</s> (self-study of the seers). 2.7.28: When completed, taking fresh <s>kuśa</s> grass, having made a pit at the root with an ox [horn], he pours water onto the <s>kuśa</s> grass [at each] hymn. 2.7.29: Remaining and fasting for the rest of the day.

body.translated_text: ŚGS 2.8.1: In the afternoon, having begged for parched grains (<s>akṣata</s>) and roasted grains (<s>dhānā</s>), he should offer into the fire with his hand according to the rule for ghee oblations, [reciting] '<s>sadasas patim adbhutam</s>' ('The wonderful lord of the assembly') — with each verse and with the remainder of the hymn. 2.8.2: He should bid the <s>ācārya</s> farewell (<s>svasti</s>) with food offerings (<s>bhakṣas</s>).

body.translated_text: ŚGS 2.9.0: Now, the <s>saṃdhyā-upāsana</s> (twilight worship). 2.9.1: In the wilderness, with fuel-stick (<s>samidh</s>) in hand, he sits at the twilight — always silent, facing northwest, in a suitable place, until the stars become visible. 2.9.2: When [the time for twilight worship] has passed, having recited the <s>Mahāvyāhṛtis</s> (great utterances), the <s>Sāvitrī</s>, and the <s>svastyayanas</s> (benedictory formulas). 2.9.3: Likewise in the morning, facing east, standing, until the disc [of the sun] becomes visible.

body.translated_text: ŚGS 2.10.0: Now, the fire rite (<s>agnikārya</s>). ŚGS 2.10.1: When [the sun] has risen, [there is] the study (<s>prādhyāyana</s>). ŚGS 2.10.2: Day after day, evening and morning. ŚGS 2.10.3: Having set up the fire, swept around, sprinkled around, and bent the right knee (?). ŚGS 2.10.4: 'I have brought a fuel-stick (<s>samidh</s>) to <s>Agni</s>, to the great <s>Jātavedas</s>. May <s>Jātavedas</s> grant me faith (<s>śraddhā</s>) and wisdom (<s>medhā</s>). <s>Svāhā</s>. You are fuel; may we prosper. You are a match; you are splendor; place splendor in me. <s>Svāhā</s>. / Being kindled, prosper me with offspring and wealth. <s>Svāhā</s>. // This is your fuel-stick, O <s>Agni</s>; by it, may you increase and be filled. May we also increase and be filled. <s>Svāhā</s>.' Thus. ŚGS 2.10.5: Then, having sprinkled around. ŚGS 2.10.6: 'May <s>Agni</s> [grant] faith and wisdom, unfailing memory to me. May this praised <s>Jātavedas</s> grant us prosperity' — with this [<s>mantra</s>] one attends upon the fire. ŚGS 2.10.7: (As declared in the <s>Sauparṇa vrata</s>, seen and practiced in the tradition of the elders: the <s>tryāyuṣa</s> [rite], with five <s>mantras</s> — one <s>mantra</s> each on the forehead, the heart, the right shoulder, the left [shoulder], and then on the back — in these five [places], one makes the <s>tripuṇḍra</s> mark with ashes.) ŚGS 2.10.8: He who, having thus offered and attended upon the fire, studies one, two, three, or all of these <s>Vedas</s>.

body.translated_text: ŚGS 2.11.0: Now, the rite of the <s>Śukriya</s> vow (<s>śukriya-vrata-karma</s>). ŚGS 2.11.1: Now, the instruction of the vow (<s>vrata-ādeśana</s>). ŚGS 2.11.2: Its procedure has been explained through the <s>upanayana</s> (initiation). ŚGS 2.11.3: He does not recite the <s>Sāvitrī</s>. ŚGS 2.11.4: Some [say] up to the giving of the staff (<s>daṇḍa-pradāna</s>). ŚGS 2.11.5: During the northward course [of the sun], in the bright fortnight (<s>śukla-pakṣa</s>). ŚGS 2.11.6: Having undertaken the <s>brahmacārya</s> of the <s>Hotṛ</s> priest, the <s>ācārya</s> (teacher) abstaining from meat [acts as] a <s>brahmacārin</s>. ŚGS 2.11.7: Avoiding the fourteenth [<s>tithi</s>] and the eighth. ŚGS 2.11.8: And some [say] the first and the last [days as well]. ŚGS 2.11.9: Or on whatever other [day] one considers auspicious by <s>nakṣatra</s> (lunar mansion), on that [day] one should instruct the <s>brahmacārya</s> for the <s>Śukriya</s> [vow]. ŚGS 2.11.10: One should observe <s>brahmacārya</s> for three nights, twelve nights, a year, or as long as the <s>guru</s> (teacher) deems [fit]. ŚGS 2.11.11: But for the <s>Śākvara</s> [vow], a year. ŚGS 2.11.12: And likewise for the <s>Vrātika</s> and <s>Aupaniṣadha</s> [vows]. ŚGS 2.11.13: When the prescribed period has been completed, the <s>brahmacārya</s> observed, at the conclusion of the <s>Bārhaspatya</s> [rite] of the <s>Śamyos</s> [recitation], when the <s>Veda</s> has been recited, intending to make [the student] hear the secret doctrine (<s>rahasya</s>), one should approach [the teacher] according to the instruction regarding the time-regulation.

body.translated_text: ŚGS 2.12.0: Now, the <s>udīkṣaṇikā</s> (observance for the transmission of sacred texts). 2.12.1: After the morning meal, in the afternoon, in the unconquered (<s>aparājitā</s>) direction [i.e., the northeast]. 2.12.2: Having offered oblations, the teacher then questions him regarding those very deities by whom he has been surrounded: 'In [the presence of] <s>Agni</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Āditya</s>, and the <s>Viśvedevas</s>—has your <s>brahmacarya</s> (student vow) been observed?' 2.12.3: When he replies: 'It has been observed, sir.' 2.12.4: Standing behind the fire, in front of the teacher, facing east, the teacher wraps him three times clockwise with an unworn garment. 2.12.5: Having made fringes above, so that it does not slip off. 2.12.6: 'For three nights, [observe] the placing of fuel-sticks, begging of alms, sleeping on the ground, and service to the teacher; being restrained in speech, vigilant—dwell in the forest, at a temple, or at the <s>Agnihotra</s>.' 2.12.7: Here some teach those same observances to one who is keeping them, at night itself. 2.12.8: The teacher abstains from meat and observes <s>brahmacarya</s>. 2.12.9: When the three nights are completed, or [during the day], going out of the village, he should not look at these causes for suspension of study: 2.12.10: Raw meat, a <s>caṇḍāla</s>, a woman who has recently given birth, a menstruating woman, a eunuch, a cremation ground, and all forms of corpses—which should not enter his mouth; he should cast off his own garments. 2.12.11: Going forth in the northeastern direction, in a clean place, the teacher seats himself facing east. 2.12.12: After sunrise, according to the rule of recitation, he recites to the silent one wearing a turban. 2.12.13: This observance applies specifically to the <s>Mahānāmnīs</s> (great names/hymns). 2.12.14: In the subsequent sections, while the teacher conducts his own self-study (<s>svādhyāya</s>), the other [student] listens. 2.12.15: He gives as <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (fee): the turban, a vessel, and a cow. 2.12.16: [He recites] '<s>tvaṃ tam</s>' and '<s>divi</s>' aloud, or everything with the <s>praṇava</s> (Oṃ). 2.12.17: Here some prepare a <s>vaiśvadeva</s> porridge (<s>caru</s>) in all sections. 2.12.18: 'As prescribed'—thus <s>Māṇḍūkeya</s>.

body.translated_text: ŚGS 2.13.0: Now, the rules regarding the staff (<s>daṇḍa</s>). 2.13.1: Now, henceforth, the rules regarding the staff. 2.13.2: One should not pass between oneself and one's staff. 2.13.3: And if the staff, girdle (<s>mekhalā</s>), or sacred thread (<s>upavīta</s>) should break or be severed, the expiation for that is the same as for [the breaking of] the chariot at the wedding. 2.13.4: If the girdle cannot be joined, having made a new one, he recites the consecration <s>mantra</s>: 2.13.5: 'O <s>Sarasvatī</s>, goddess who knows the distinction between pure and impure, O protectress, O girdle—unspilt, uncut, extend my vow. You, O <s>Agni</s>, bearer of vows, pure <s>Agni</s>, bring the gods here; bring to our sacrifice the offering; bearing the vows, drinker of vows, inviolable, be our messenger, ageless, rich in heroes; bestowing treasures, gracious <s>Agni</s>, O <s>Jātavedas</s>, protect us for life.' 2.13.6: And he ties the sacred thread to the staff. 2.13.7: And regarding this [it is said]: 2.13.8: 'The sacred thread, staff, girdle, and skin—when the vow is complete, one should offer them into the water with a verse to <s>Varuṇa</s>, or with a juice-offering.'

body.translated_text: ŚGS 2.14.0: Now, the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> (offering to all gods) rite. 2.14.1: Now, the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>. 2.14.2: The procedure for the oblation (<s>homa</s>) has been explained [above]. 2.14.3: When the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> [food] is cooked, one should offer in the domestic fire (<s>gṛhya agni</s>), in the evening and morning. 2.14.4: "To <s>Agni</s>, <s>svāhā</s>; to <s>Soma</s>, <s>svāhā</s>; to <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>, <s>svāhā</s>; to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>svāhā</s>; to <s>Bharadvāja Dhanvantari</s>, <s>svāhā</s>; to all the gods (<s>Viśve Devāḥ</s>), <s>svāhā</s>; to <s>Prajāpati</s>, <s>svāhā</s>; to <s>Aditi</s>, <s>svāhā</s>; to <s>Anumati</s>, <s>svāhā</s>; to <s>Agni Sviṣṭakṛt</s> (the fire that has offered well), <s>svāhā</s>"—having offered to these deities. 2.14.5: Then, in the middle of the dwelling, he should carry the <s>bali</s> (food offering) to these same deities, and [saying] "Homage to <s>Brahman</s> and to the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>; O lord of the dwelling (<s>Vāstoṣpati</s>), acknowledge us"—[offering] in the middle of the dwelling to <s>Vāstoṣpati</s> as well. 2.14.6: Then, going clockwise around the directions, he carries the <s>bali</s> offering in the appropriate manner. 2.14.7: "Homage to <s>Indra</s> and the <s>Aindras</s>; homage to <s>Yama</s> and the <s>Yāmyas</s>; homage to <s>Varuṇa</s> and the <s>Vāruṇas</s>; homage to <s>Soma</s> and the <s>Saumyas</s>; homage to <s>Bṛhaspati</s> and the <s>Bārhaspatyas</s>." 2.14.8: Then, in the circle of the sun: "Homage to <s>Aditi</s> and the <s>Ādityas</s>; homage to the <s>nakṣatras</s> (lunar mansions), the seasons (<s>ṛtu</s>), the months, the half-months, the days-and-nights, and the years." 2.14.9: "To <s>Pūṣan</s>, to <s>Pathikṛt</s> (the path-maker), to <s>Dhātṛ</s>, to <s>Vidhātṛ</s>, and to the <s>Maruts</s>"—[these are offered] at the thresholds (<s>dehalī</s>). 2.14.10: "To <s>Viṣṇu</s>"—at the grinding-stone (<s>dṛṣad</s>). 2.14.11: "To the lord of trees (<s>Vanaspati</s>)"—at the mortar (<s>ulūkhala</s>). 2.14.12: "To the herbs (<s>oṣadhī</s>)"—at the place of the herbs. 2.14.13: "To <s>Parjanya</s> [and] to the Waters"—at the water jar (<s>maṇi</s>). 2.14.14: "Homage to <s>Śrī</s>"—at the bed; at the head [of the bed]; at the feet, to <s>Bhadrakālī</s>. 2.14.15: In a concealed place: "Homage to the deity of all food (<s>sarvānnabhūta</s>)." 2.14.16: Then, in the open air: "To the night-wanderers (<s>naktaṃcara</s>)"—in the evening; "To the day-wanderers (<s>ahaścara</s>)"—in the morning; and [reciting] "O gods (<s>ye devāsaḥ</s>)." 2.14.17: To the unknown deities, to the north; and to the lord of wealth (<s>Dhanapati</s>). 2.14.18: With the sacred thread worn over the right shoulder (<s>prācīnāvītin</s>), he pours the remainder to the south, [reciting] "Those who were consumed by fire (<s>ye agnidagdhāḥ</s>)." 2.14.19: Having given to gods, ancestors, and men, he should feed a learned <s>brāhmaṇa</s> (<s>śrotriya</s>). 2.14.20: Or he should give alms to a <s>brahmacārin</s>. 2.14.21: Then he should feed a married woman (<s>sauvāsinī</s>), a pregnant woman, children, and the elderly. 2.14.22: For the dogs, for the <s>śvapacas</s> (outcasts), and for the birds, he should place [food] on the ground. 2.14.23: Thus, one should not eat what has not been [first] distributed. 2.14.24: Nor [should one eat] alone. 2.14.25: Nor before [distributing]. 2.14.26: On this, the <s>ṛc</s> (verse) has been spoken: "In vain does the foolish one obtain food."

body.translated_text: ŚGS 2.15.0: Now, the rite of the six [recipients of] <s>arghya</s> (respectful reception). 2.15.1: If any one of the six worthy of <s>arghya</s> should arrive—a cow, a goat, or food—whatever one considers most appropriate, that one should prepare. 2.15.2: The <s>arghya</s> reception should not be without meat. 2.15.3: One should say: "Perform [the rite] in connection with a sacrifice, in connection with a wedding." 2.15.4: For the <s>ācārya</s> (teacher), [the offering is] <s>āgneya</s> (sacred to <s>Agni</s>). 2.15.5: For the <s>ṛtvij</s> (sacrificial priest), <s>bārhaspatya</s> (sacred to <s>Bṛhaspati</s>). 2.15.6: For [a guest connected with] the wedding, <s>prājāpatya</s> (sacred to <s>Prajāpati</s>). 2.15.7: For the king, <s>aindra</s> (sacred to <s>Indra</s>). 2.15.8: For a dear friend, <s>maitra</s> (sacred to <s>Mitra</s>). 2.15.9: For a <s>snātaka</s> (one who has completed studies), <s>aindrāgna</s> (sacred to <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>). 2.15.10: Even if one would sacrifice repeatedly with <s>Soma</s> throughout the year, those who have been honored with <s>arghya</s> should perform the sacrifice for him, not those who have not been [so] honored. 2.15.11: On this, it is also [said]:

body.translated_text: ŚGS 2.16.0: Now, the rite concerning animals (<s>paśukarma</s>). 2.16.1: 'In the <s>madhuparka</s> (honey-mixture reception), in the <s>Soma</s> ritual, and in rites for the ancestors and deities—only in these should animals be slain, and not elsewhere,' so declared <s>Manu</s>. 2.16.2: 'The teacher, the father, both, a friend, and an unexpected guest in the house—whatever they ordain, that one should do; thus is the <s>dharma</s> enjoined.' 2.16.3: 'One should know as a guest [only] one who is not from the same village, who has come from a journey, and who has arrived at the house where there is a wife, and where the sacred fires also are.' 2.16.4: 'The <s>Agnihotra</s> fire, the <s>bali</s>-offering animals, a guest who has arrived at the proper time, children, and the family elders—these, when dishonored, burn [the householder].' 2.16.5: 'The draft ox, the <s>Agnihotra</s>, and the <s>brahmacārin</s>—these three succeed only by eating; their success does not come from not eating.' 2.16.6: 'The domestic deities approach the householder day after day, seeking their share; one should offer to them.' ŚGS 2.17.0: Now, the rite of hospitality (<s>atithikarma</s>). 2.17.1: 'Even from one who always gleans grass and offers the <s>Agnihotra</s>, a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> dwelling [there] unhonored takes away all merit.' 2.17.2: 'One should give up to [even] a pot of water; one should offer up to [even] a piece of firewood. Up to a <s>sūkta</s> or an <s>anuvāka</s>, the <s>brahmayajña</s> (worship of sacred knowledge) is prescribed.' 2.17.3: 'There should be no fasting while on a journey; the wife maintains the vow. A son, a brother, or the wife, or a student may carry out his <s>bali</s>-offering.' 2.17.4: 'Those who perform this <s>vaiśvadeva</s> (offering to all gods) evening and morning—they prosper in wealth, lifespan, fame, and offspring.'

body.translated_text: ŚGS 2.18.0: Now, the rite for the <s>brahmacārin</s> (student) about to depart. 2.18.1: The <s>brahmacārin</s>, about to depart, takes leave of the teacher. 2.18.2: [Reciting] 'Of <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s>' in a low voice; 'Oṃ, I am about to depart, sir' aloud. 2.18.3: '<s>Prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s>, wide-extending, through you I go forth. To the god as protector I entrust [this student]. O god <s>Savitṛ</s>, this is your <s>brahmacārin</s>; to you I entrust him; protect him; do not harm him'—[he recites] in a low voice. 2.18.4: 'Oṃ, may there be welfare!'—the teacher [says] aloud. 'May there be welfare!'—the teacher [says] aloud.

body.translated_text: ŚGS 3.1.0: Now, the <s>samāvartana</s> (return/graduation ceremony). 3.1.1: The bath is for one who is about to return [from studentship]. 3.1.2: As has been stated regarding the draft ox: having seated him in that [place], he shaves his hair, beard, body hair, and nails. 3.1.3: Having rubbed [the body] with rice, barley, sesame, mustard, and <s>apāmārga</s> plants, always with flowers. 3.1.4: Having bathed [him] with the <s>Āpohiṣṭhīya</s> hymn ('O waters, you are indeed'). 3.1.5: Having adorned [him]. 3.1.6: [Reciting] 'You two garments (<s>yuvam vastrāṇi</s>),' he puts on the two garments. 3.1.7: Then he ties a gold ornament (<s>niṣka</s>) on him, [reciting] 'For long life, for splendor (<s>āyuṣyam varcasyam</s>).' 3.1.8: [Reciting] 'Mine, O <s>Agni</s>, is the splendor (<s>mama agne varcaḥ</s>),' [he ties on] the turban. 3.1.9: [Reciting] 'House to house (<s>gṛhaṃ gṛham</s>),' [he puts on further adornments].

body.translated_text: ŚGS 3.2.0: Now, the house rite (<s>gṛhakarma</s>). ŚGS 3.2.1: One who is about to build a house, [saying] 'Here I encompass the settlements for the eating of food,' having drawn a line three times with a branch of an <s>udumbara</s> (fig) tree, offers on the prepared ground (<s>sthaṇḍila</s>) in the middle. ŚGS 3.2.2: 'Who are you? Whose are you? For what purpose? One desirous of a settlement offers. <s>Svāhā</s>. In this [place] is the allotted portion of the gods. From here the ancestors were born and have departed. <s>Virāj</s> offered; one desirous of a settlement [offers], not withholding anything of the gods. <s>Svāhā</s>.' Thus. ŚGS 3.2.3: Having had the post-holes dug. ŚGS 3.2.4: Having poured water-churnings into [them]. ŚGS 3.2.5: 'I set up this branch of immortality, a stream of honey, a means of crossing to wealth. May the child cry towards it, the boy; may the cow low towards it, her calf always [present]' — with this [verse], he places a branch of <s>udumbara</s> smeared with ghee in the right door-post hole. ŚGS 3.2.6: 'I raise up this branch of the world, a stream of honey, a means of crossing to wealth. May the child cry towards it, the boy; may the cow low towards it, her young calf' — thus on the northern [side]. ŚGS 3.2.7: Thus for each pair, on the south, behind, and on the north. ŚGS 3.2.9: 'This branch of this tree, dripping with ghee, I set in the immortal. May the child cry towards it, the boy; may the milk-cows flow towards it, their calf always [present]' — thus he raises the king-post (<s>sthūṇā-rāja</s>). ŚGS 3.2.9: 'May a young boy, a calf, come to it, O lord of the world; may [people] come to it with jars of filtered [liquor], with vessels of curds.'

body.translated_text: ŚGS 3.3.1: 'Stand firm right here, O pillar, steadfast, rich in horses, rich in cattle, rich in ornaments. Stand in safety, dripping with ghee. Stand right here, well-set, abounding [in goods], rich in grain. In the midst of prosperity, be satisfied; may evil-doers not reach you. Invited here are the cows, invited are the goats and sheep. And the sweet essence of food is invited in our house. Be established on the <s>Rathantara</s> [<s>sāman</s>]; rest upon the <s>Vāmadeva</s> [<s>sāman</s>]; be supported by the <s>Bṛhatī</s> [meter]' — thus he touches the king-post (<s>sthūṇā-rāja</s>). ŚGS 3.3.2: He touches the posts of the [house with] measured [proportions]. ŚGS 3.3.3: 'Truth and Faith' — [he recites at] the eastern [posts]. ŚGS 3.3.4: 'Sacrifice and the Priestly Fee (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>)' — [at] the southern [posts]. ŚGS 3.3.5: 'Strength and Vigor' — [at] the western [posts]. ŚGS 3.3.6: 'Sacred Knowledge (<s>Brahman</s>) and Ruling Power (<s>Kṣatra</s>)' — [at] the northern [posts]. ŚGS 3.3.7: 'Prosperity (<s>Śrī</s>) [is] the dome (<s>stūpa</s>); <s>Dharma</s> [is] the king-post (<s>sthūṇā-rāja</s>).' ŚGS 3.3.8: 'Day and Night [are] the door-planks.' ŚGS 3.3.9: 'The Year [is] the covering (roof).' ŚGS 3.3.10: [Reciting] '<s>ukṣā samudra</s>' ('The bull [is] the ocean'), he should bury a smeared stone beneath the dome (<s>stūpa</s>).

body.translated_text: ŚGS 3.4.0: Now, the rite of entering a house (<s>gṛha-praveśa-karma</s>). 3.4.1: In the rite pertaining to <s>Vāstoṣpati</s>. 3.4.2: Having placed the domestic fire (<s>gṛhya agni</s>) outside, [reciting:] "I place the fire with an auspicious mind; may this be the meeting-place of riches. Do not harm us, neither the old nor the young; be auspicious to our two-footed and four-footed [creatures]." 3.4.3: Having placed a new water-pot on fresh <s>kuśa</s> grass with tips pointing east, 3.4.4: having consecrated [it] with [the verse:] "May our heroes be unharmed; may our wealth not be poured away." 3.4.5: With the <s>stotriya</s> (praise-hymn) of the <s>Rathantara</s>, arranged in <s>kakubh</s> form to make three verses, he offers in the forenoon. 3.4.6: [With that] of the <s>Vāmadevya</s> at midday. 3.4.7: [With that] of the <s>Bṛhat</s> in the afternoon. 3.4.8: The four great <s>vyāhṛtis</s> (sacred utterances), three [verses beginning with] "O <s>Vāstoṣpati</s>," [the verse] "O <s>Vāstoṣpati</s>, remover of disease," [the verse] "O <s>Vāstoṣpati</s>, firm is the pillar" — the <s>sauviṣṭakṛt</s> (offering to Agni Sviṣṭakṛt) being the tenth — [these are offered] with a <s>sthālīpāka</s> (cooked oblation) at night. 3.4.9: Taking his eldest son and wife, together with grain, he should enter. 3.4.10: [Reciting:] "These are the auspicious houses of <s>Indra</s>, rich in wealth and protection; I approach them together with my wife, together with my offspring, together with my cattle, together with the increase of wealth, together with whatever I have."

body.translated_text: ŚGS 3.5.1: When leaving the village, [he recites:] "Auspicious, auspicious, peaceful, peaceful — for safety and for peace I approach you. May there be no fear for us. May the village not hand me over to the forest; O all-great one, do not abandon me." 3.5.2: When entering the village, not empty-handed, [he recites:] "May the forest not hand me over to the village; O great one, to the all, do not abandon me." 3.5.3: [Reciting:] "I approach the auspicious houses, cheerful, not slaying heroes, most heroic, rich in heroes; bearing refreshment, sprinkling ghee — may I, cheerful, settle among others" — this should always be recited.

body.translated_text: ŚGS 3.6.0: Now, the sacrifice for one about to journey (<s>pravasad-yajanam</s>). 3.6.1: One who has not established the sacred fires (<s>anāhitāgni</s>), about to travel, looks at his house. 3.6.2: [He recites:] "O <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, guard these my houses, you two; undestroyed and unscattered — may <s>Pūṣan</s> protect them until our return." 3.6.3: And he mutters, "We have reached the path."

ŚGS_3.7.5: virājo.doho.asi.virājo.doham.aśīya.mayi.padyāyai.virājo.doha.iti.pādya.pratigrahaṇaḥ /
body.translated_text: ŚGS 3.7.1: Now, having traveled, on returning, he looks at his house. 3.7.2: [He recites:] "O houses, do not fear, do not tremble; we come bearing nourishment. Bearing nourishment, cheerful, wise, I approach the houses with a rejoicing mind — those over which one presides when away, in which there is much good cheer. We call upon the houses; may they who know recognize us. Invited hither are the cows, invited are the goats and sheep; and the essence of food is invited into our houses." 3.7.3: Having approached the domestic fire (<s>gṛhya agni</s>), [he recites:] "This our fire is blessed, this is most blessed of all; by attending upon it, may we not come to harm; may it establish us in excellence." 3.7.4: He should speak auspicious words. 3.7.5: When receiving the foot-washing water (<s>pādya</s>), [he recites:] "You are the milk of <s>Virāj</s>; may I partake of the milk of <s>Virāj</s>. For my nourishment, O milk of <s>Virāj</s>."

body.translated_text: ŚGS 3.8.0: Now, the <s>āgrayaṇa</s> (first-fruits offering). 3.8.1: One who has not established the [śrauta] fires, when about to eat the new [grain], should offer in the domestic fire (<s>gṛhya agni</s>) to the <s>āgrayaṇa</s> deities, with the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s> as the fourth, with the <s>svāhā</s>-utterance. 3.8.2: 'For <s>Prajāpati</s>, I take thee as the offering. For my prosperity, for my glory, for my nourishment'—having recited [this] over what is intended for eating. 3.8.3: 'The gods have led us to auspicious fortune; may we partake of thee who art possessed of life. Be thou nourishing to us, O father, enter us; be thou auspicious to the two-footed, auspicious to the four-footed'—sprinkling with water, he eats three times. 3.8.4: 'You are sustenance (<s>ama</s>); O breath (<s>prāṇa</s>), I speak the truth. You are sustenance; you have entered all. Driving away old age and disease from my body, remain with me. Do not harm [me], O <s>Indra</s>'—he touches the region of the heart. 3.8.5: 'You are the navel; do not fear. You are the knot of the vital breaths; do not come undone'—[he touches] the navel. 3.8.6: 'May we hear with our ears what is auspicious'—according to the sign [of the verse]. 3.8.7: [Reciting] 'That eye (<s>tac cakṣuḥ</s>),' he worships the sun.
